quick: 10 mg orally about 60 minutes before sexual activity, as needed; range 5-20 mg, max once daily
May be taken with or without food; high-fat meals may slow onset
Not indicated in women; pregnancy category not applicable (male use)
No adjustment for mild-moderate impairment; not studied in severe (dialysis); use with caution
Moderate impairment (Child-Pugh B): start 5 mg, max 10 mg; avoid in severe (Child-Pugh C)
Both are vasodilators - combined use may increase orthostatic hypotension
Blood pressure, cardiovascular fitness for sexual activity, vision/hearing changes
summary: Vardenafil is a potent, selective PDE5 inhibitor used as-needed for erectile dysfunction. By blocking PDE5 it raises cyclic GMP in penile smooth muscle, enhancing nitric-oxide-mediated erection during sexual stimulation. It is contraindicated with nitrates and with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat because of dangerous hypotension, and it can prolong the QT interval. Dose reduction is needed with CYP3A4 inhibitors, alpha-blockers, and moderate hepatic impairment.
indications: Treatment of erectile dysfunction in adult men

dosage.d: 10 mg approximately 60 minutes before sexual activity; adjust to 20 mg or 5 mg by response/tolerability
dosage.n: Requires sexual stimulation; max one tablet per day

dosage.d: Start 5 mg; do not exceed 10 mg

Ritonavir/cobicistat: max 2.5 mg/72 h; indinavir, saquinavir, atazanavir, ketoconazole/itraconazole 400 mg, clarithromycin: max 2.5 mg/24 h; ketoconazole/itraconazole 200 mg, erythromycin: max 5 mg/24 h

admin: Take approximately 60 minutes before anticipated sexual activity
Do not take more than once per day
moa: During sexual stimulation, nitric oxide is released in the corpus cavernosum and activates guanylate cyclase, increasing cyclic GMP, which relaxes smooth muscle and increases penile blood flow to produce an erection. Vardenafil selectively inhibits PDE5, the enzyme that degrades cGMP, thereby prolonging and enhancing cGMP-mediated smooth-muscle relaxation. Without sexual stimulation there is no effect because nitric oxide release is required.

absolute: Concurrent use of nitrates or nitric oxide donors (in any form, regular or intermittent)
Concurrent use of guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat
relative: Cardiovascular disease where sexual activity is inadvisable
Congenital QT prolongation or use of Class IA/III antiarrhythmics
Anatomic penile deformity or conditions predisposing to priapism (sickle cell, multiple myeloma, leukemia)
History of NAION; bleeding disorders / active peptic ulcer
monitor: Cardiovascular status before initiating sexual activity

preg: Vardenafil is intended for use in men and is not indicated in women; pregnancy considerations are not applicable.
lact: Not applicable - vardenafil is intended for use in men.
renal: No dose adjustment is needed for mild to moderate renal impairment. It has not been studied in patients on renal dialysis or with severe renal impairment; use with caution.
hepatic: In moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh B), start at 5 mg and do not exceed 10 mg. Vardenafil has not been evaluated in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) and is not recommended.

major: Nitrates / nitric oxide donors (life-threatening hypotension - contraindicated)
Riociguat and other guanylate cyclase stimulators (severe hypotension - contraindicated)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, cobicistat, ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin) - raise vardenafil levels; dose-limit
Class IA (quinidine, procainamide) or Class III (amiodarone, sotalol) antiarrhythmics - additive QT prolongation
moderate: Alpha-blockers (symptomatic hypotension - start 5 mg, stabilize alpha-blocker first)
interactions.food: Grapefruit juice may increase plasma levels; high-fat meals reduce Cmax and slow onset
interactions.alcohol: Both vardenafil and alcohol are mild vasodilators; combined use may augment blood-pressure-lowering effects
interactions.diagnostics: Can prolong the QTc interval on ECG

serious: Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (sudden vision loss)
emergency: Sudden vision loss in one or both eyes

monitoring: Cardiovascular suitability for sexual activity before starting
Blood pressure, especially with alpha-blockers or antihypertensives
counsel: Take about 1 hour before sexual activity; it works only with sexual stimulation
Never use with nitrates (e.g., nitroglycerin) or riociguat - this can cause a dangerous drop in blood pressure
Seek emergency care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours
Stop the drug and seek care for sudden vision or hearing loss
Do not exceed one dose per day
Tell your doctor about heart disease and all other medicines, including chest-pain drugs
pk: Median peak plasma concentration about 60 minutes (range 30 minutes to 2 hours) when fasting
Clinical effect generally up to about 4-5 hours
Store at controlled room temperature 25 C; protect from excessive heat and moisture
pearls: Contraindicated with nitrates and with guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat) due to severe hypotension
Can prolong the QT interval - avoid in congenital long QT and with Class IA/III antiarrhythmics
Highly CYP3A4-metabolized; strong inhibitors require strict dose limits
Sudden vision loss (NAION) and sudden hearing loss are rare but warrant immediate discontinuation
Absolute bioavailability is only about 15% due to extensive first-pass metabolism
missed: Vardenafil is used on an as-needed basis before sexual activity, so there is no fixed dosing schedule and no missed dose to make up. Do not take more than one dose in any 24-hour period.
overdose: Single doses up to 80 mg or repeated doses caused back pain, abnormal vision, or muscle aches in studies. Manage supportively; standard measures to support cardiovascular status. Because vardenafil is highly protein-bound, dialysis is unlikely to accelerate clearance.
